source_of_truth: histories/*.md; the key is a proposed interpretation, not an extra source for participants

questions.query: At the cutoff, which of A, B and C are bench-ready under the current rule? Identify the eligible set and briefly explain why each other station is not ready.
required: C alone is bench-ready under v2.
A has buffering disabled and lacks current firmware-8 packet and latency evidence.
B's unchanged 7.5-hour pack fails the eight-hour minimum.
unsupported_traps: Treating A's old badge as current evidence.
Saying B fails the old five-second latency rule under v2.
Treating the ordered pack as installed.

questions.query: Does the record show that A failed the current packet-success criterion after its firmware upgrade, or is that performance unknown? State what happened to the earlier packet result.
required: Current packet performance is unknown, with no firmware-8 packet test.
The 99/100 firmware-7 result was valid earlier but cannot establish current firmware-8 packet performance.
unsupported_traps: Converting absence of a current test into an observed packet failure.
Claiming the upgrade preserves the old packet performance.

questions.query: Suppose B's pack is replaced and a valid new test establishes 8.5 hours, with all its other recorded attributes unchanged. Under the current rule, what is the new bench-ready set? Explain any change.
required: B and C are now bench-ready; A still is not.
B's pack change resolves its remaining v2 deficit; its packet rate, six-second latency and enabled buffer meet v2.
unsupported_traps: Keeping B excluded using superseded v1 latency.
Promoting A because B improved.

questions.query: Using the accepted current calibration, how many unique samples are late, out of how many unique samples? Name the late sample or samples.
required: One of three unique samples is late: U.
The evaluation uses the calibrated gateway arrival and counts U-retry as U, not as another sample.
unsupported_traps: Four displayed rows become four unique failures.
Using database insertion as gateway arrival.

questions.query: Were S and T simultaneous at acquisition or at gateway arrival? Give their gateway arrival times on the reference clock under the accepted current calibration.
required: They were simultaneous at neither acquisition nor gateway arrival.
Reference gateway arrival is 101 for S and 101.5 for T; their common database insertion time does not imply simultaneous acquisition or arrival.
unsupported_traps: Treating one database batch as one acquisition time.
Adding the signed offset instead of subtracting it.

questions.query: Replace the exact calibration only for this hypothetical: the gateway is ahead by one common unknown offset in the closed interval [2,4] seconds. Which unique samples are guaranteed to pass, guaranteed to fail, or unresolved under the two-second requirement? Is it possible that all three pass?
required: S and T are guaranteed passes, with possible delays [0,2].
No sample is a guaranteed failure; U is unresolved with possible delay [2,4].
All three can pass at offset 4, but an all-pass outcome is not guaranteed.
unsupported_traps: Treating equality at two seconds as failure.
Saying U is guaranteed late based on the superseded exact-offset assumption.
Choosing different offsets for different samples.

questions.query: Does selected candidate C1 pass the finite acceptance rule at the cutoff? Give its pass, failure and untested counts, naming the failed and untested cases.
required: C1 does not pass.
There are 9 passes, 2 failures (A8 and B3), and 1 untested case (B4).
The all-cases-evaluated and at-least-11-passes requirement is not satisfied.
unsupported_traps: Replacing C1's B3 failure with C2's result.
Calling untested B4 a failure.
Using the success-only export as the cohort.

questions.query: For C1, what are the pass fractions among evaluated cohort cases and among all authorized cohort cases? Explain why neither denominator is the original fourteen-file inventory.
required: 9/11 among evaluated cohort cases and 9/12 among all authorized cohort cases (equivalent percentages accepted).
X1 and X2 were excluded before evaluation; the authorized cohort has twelve, of which B4 is untested.
unsupported_traps: Using 9/9 from the filtered illustrations.
Excluding observed failures after outcomes are known.

questions.query: If the project now selects C2 without performing any additional evaluations, what are C2's pass, failure and untested counts for the authorized cohort, and does it pass the acceptance rule?
required: C2 has 1 pass (B3), 0 observed failures and 11 untested cases.
Acceptance is not established; C1's outcomes cannot fill C2's missing evaluations.
unsupported_traps: Inheriting nine C1 passes.
Calling eleven untested cases eleven failures.
Claiming that C2 would fail every missing evaluation.

questions.query: May the live source be retired at the cutoff under the supplied rule? How many current source keys have verified matching current revisions, and which keys still prevent establishing complete coverage?
required: No; 93 of the 97 current source keys have verified matching current revisions.
K95 and K96 lack the M0 audit; K97 revision 1 and K12 revision 2 have no destination ingestion or verification record.
Missing verification is not an observed mismatch.
unsupported_traps: Counting K12 revision 1 as verification of its current revision 2.
Equating accepted ingestion with checksum verification.

questions.query: How many distinct stored backup objects do the labels backup-east and archive-copy establish? Does that stored content include the post-M0 addition and revision change?
required: The labels establish one stored object, object-amber, because they are aliases.
It contains M0 only and omits K97 and K12 revision 2 (it has K12 revision 1).
unsupported_traps: Two names imply two independent copies.
A snapshot silently tracks later source writes.

questions.query: Suppose only the two missing M0 comparisons now complete and verify K95 and K96 revision 1. Nothing else changes. May the source now be retired? Give the updated current-revision verification count and remaining blockers.
required: No; 95 of 97 current keys are now verified at current revisions.
K97 revision 1 and K12 revision 2 still lack destination synchronization and verification.
unsupported_traps: Complete verification of an old snapshot becomes complete verification of current source state.

questions.query: Under the final adopted caps, which feasible pair maximizes output? Give the pair, output and total use of staff, memory and power.
required: B and C, output 16, with staff 8, memory 9 and power 8.
The pair meets all current caps; the higher-output A/B proposal is not feasible.
unsupported_traps: Combining individually feasible jobs without checking their sums.
Using the earlier memory cap.

questions.query: If only the staff rental is adopted, does the A/B pair become feasible? Identify any remaining resource violations using the recorded quantities.
required: No. A/B requires memory 11 against cap 9 and power 9 against cap 8.
Raising the staff cap to 10 resolves staff only (the pair uses 9).
unsupported_traps: Treating a staff-only rental as a general increase to all caps.

questions.query: Instead of the original objective, require exactly two jobs including A and add only one memory unit to the final adopted allowance. Staff and power stay unchanged, and the staff rental is not adopted. What feasible pair can be chosen, with what output and resource totals?
required: A and C can be chosen, with output 14 and staff 7, memory 10, power 7.
The changed caps are (8,10,8); B/C does not satisfy the new A-inclusion requirement.
unsupported_traps: Reusing the old optimal pair after its eligibility requirement changes.
Combining the two distinct capacity proposals without authorization.

questions.query: Is the current twenty-two-participant workshop feasible under every supplied rule? Explain the booked timing and the headphone issue as well as capacity.
required: Yes; 22 participants fit the room, 24 kits and two leaders' combined capacity of 24.
The confirmed 10:00–11:30 session fits 09:00–17:00 availability and both leaders' confirmations.
Headphones are exempt from the pre-11:00 amplified-sound restriction.
unsupported_traps: Inventing a hidden approval gate.
Applying an amplified-sound restriction to the exempt headphone activity.

questions.query: How many additional participants can the current plan accommodate separately under the room cap, kit inventory and leader ratio? What is the overall remaining participant capacity?
required: Room, kits and leader ratio each have capacity for 2 additional participants.
The overall remaining participant capacity is 2; the capacities are simultaneous limits and are not added.
unsupported_traps: Adding three separate spare counts to claim room for six.
Counting leaders as participants or as kit users despite the supplied rules.

questions.query: If exactly two more participants register and nothing else changes, is the workshop still feasible? State the new count and how it relates to the three capacity limits.
required: Yes; 24 participants exactly meet the room cap, 24-kit inventory and two-leader capacity.
The booked time and headphone exemption remain valid.
unsupported_traps: Treating equality with a capacity limit as a violation.
Requiring an extra leader when the exact twelve-per-leader rule still holds.
